claim: The four-observable inconsistency (chi2=45.95, 2 dof) is carried by a single observable, not by the two-state model itself
predicts: leave-one-out chi2 for at least one removal falls below 4.0 on 1 dof
falsifies: every removal leaves chi2 > 4 -> the two-state model is what is broken, not a measurement

claim: The anisotropy constraint |cos a|=0.66 is soft: it rests on the assumption that both chromophores are excited with equal probability (w=1/2), not on the detuning
predicts: the crystal register alpha=110.4 deg is reachable at some w in [0,1]; report the w that reaches it
falsifies: alpha stays above 125 deg for all w -> the anisotropy genuinely demands 131.3 and the geometry is wrong

claim: CD splitting and superradiance demand incompatible detunings (253 vs 1281 cm-1) only because the apparent->true splitting inversion saturates: a large true Delta can still produce the observed apparent 261.58 cm-1
predicts: the apparent-splitting curve is flat to within 30 cm-1 across true Delta = 250-1300, i.e. apparent splitting does not discriminate them
falsifies: apparent splitting tracks true Delta monotonically over that range -> the two observables are genuinely contradictory and one is wrong
